title: De transformatione serierum in fractiones continuas, ubi simul haec theoria non mediocriter amplificatur

deep.reconstruction:
This page applies Theorem II (§23, previous page) to three examples. Theorem II says: if s = 1/(ab) − 1/(bc) + 1/(cd) − 1/(de) + …, then 1/(as) = b + ab/(c−a + bc/(d−b + cd/(e−c + …))). The aim is to show that this form gives continued fractions quite different from those of Theorem I.

§24, log 2. Euler subtracts 1 from l2 = 1 − 1/2 + 1/3 − … and adds the resulting series term by term to the original. Pairing equal-index terms gives 2 l2 − 1 = 1/(1·2) − 1/(2·3) + 1/(3·4) − …. With a,b,c,… = 1,2,3,… this yields
1/(2 ln2 − 1) = 2 + 1·2/(2 + 2·3/(2 + 3·4/(2 + …))).

§25, π. The same trick on π/4 = 1 − 1/3 + 1/5 − … gives π/2 − 1 = Σ ± 2/((2k−1)(2k+1)). Hence π/4 − 1/2 = 1/(1·3) − 1/(3·5) + 1/(5·7) − …. With a,b,c,… = 1,3,5,… this yields
4/(π − 2) = 3 + 1·3/(4 + 3·5/(4 + 5·7/(4 + …))).

§26, general case. Let Δ = ∫_0^1 x^{m−1} dx/(1+x^n) = 1/m − 1/(m+n) + 1/(m+2n) − … (cf. §20). Adding Δ − 1/m to Δ term by term gives
2Δ − 1/m = n/(m(m+n)) − n/((m+n)(m+2n)) + ….
So s = (2mΔ − 1)/(mn), with a = m, b = m+n, c = m+2n, …. Theorem II then gives
n/(2mΔ − 1) = m + n + m(m+n)/(2n + (m+n)(m+2n)/(2n + (m+2n)(m+3n)/(2n + …))).
The special cases (m,n) = (1,1) and (1,2) recover §24 and §25.

In modern terms this is the Euler (series-to-continued-fraction) correspondence, applied to a telescoped form of the alternating series. The general case is a continued fraction for a value of 2F1(1, m/n; 1+m/n; −1). The aim is to obtain continued fractions with constant partial denominators, analogous to Brouncker's.
errors: No mathematical errors. All three identities check algebraically.
The continued fractions are numerically plausible: 1/(2ln2−1) ≈ 2.5887 and 4/(π−2) ≈ 3.5039.

Convergence is not discussed, but it holds by the Seidel–Stern criterion: the partial numerators grow like k², the denominators are constant, and the equivalent elements c_k ~ const/k, whose sum diverges.
Minor slip in the transcription (and possibly in print): the series for π/4 − 1 should end '… − 1/11 + etc.', not '− etc.'.

ideas.what: Adding an alternating series to its own shifted copy (pairing equal-index terms) to obtain an alternating series in reciprocals of products of consecutive terms
ideas.modern_name: elementary series acceleration / telescoping rearrangement (first step of the Euler transform)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine, correct worked examples of Euler's alternating-series-to-continued-fraction transformation, in a well-known published paper that is discussed in the continued-fraction historical literature (e.g. Khrushchev's book on Euler's continued fractions). There is nothing unfinished or uncredited.
